newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends lower with support intact.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends lower with support intact.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed a thinly-traded session firmer amid steady trade buying, floor sources said.

The buying offset early speculative selling which pressured the benchmark October contract to its downside target of 11.00 cents. Failing to take out support, the speculators slowed their selling and allowed the front month to climb to the day's high of 11.12 cents.
Dealers said today's positive close could attract follow-through buying on Thursday, and pegged resistance at the recent high of 11.22 cents in October.
The most-active October contract ended 0.05 cents higher at 11.11 cents, while second-position March closed up 0.04 at 11.25 cents.
The rest of the board finished 0.04 to 0.08 cent firmer.
An estimated 10,642 lots changed hands on the day compared with Tuesday's official 10,081 lots.
Open interest in October fell by 895 lots to 92,917 lots as of Tuesday. March's open interest rose by 178 lots to stand at 42,225 lots.
In fundamental news, European Union beet sugar output is expected to fall to 16.05 million tonnes in 1997/98 from 16.51 million tonnes last season, the European Commission said.
